title: MCP stdio get_record answers a missing or hidden id with uncoded error text, while the HTTP door answers RECORD_NOT_FOUND 404
body:
qa#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibw6yXcLi9aRRBpPT4W

## Reproduction (ee9ad834; reproduced twice)

1. Start the server with stdio MCP: `os start` with `OS_MCP_STDIO_ENABLED=true` and `OS_MCP_STDIO_API_KEY=an admin osk_ key`.
2. Over stdio, `tools/call get_record {objectName:"showcase_task", recordId:"qa_missing_id_123"}`.
   - Actual: `result.isError` true and `content[0].text` = `Record "qa_missing_id_123" not found in "showcase_task"`. There is no `{error:{code,status}}`.
   - An RLS-hidden id under a member key answers the same way.
3. The same call on the HTTP door (/api/v1/mcp) answers `{error:{code:"RECORD_NOT_FOUND", status:404, message}}`. Stdio `update_record` on the same missing id also answers the coded RECORD_NOT_FOUND.

Expected: the coded envelope on both doors, which is the #23509 contract: a stdio client branches on the code.

## Mechanism

`createStdioDataBridge.get` returns null by design (`packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts` ~1209: "get_record owns the not-found wording on this path"). `get_record`'s `record == null` branch then renders `errorResult(\`Record "…" not found in "…"\`)` (`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts` ~2633) instead of `errorResultWithCode`.

Impact: low. This is a residual of the closed #23509.
